preview.pick: Rosalind Franklin solved the structure of DNA on her own, and her photograph was simply stolen by her Cambridge rivals

served.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
choices: Watson and Crick deserve sole credit for the double helix because they alone were willing to build and test models
Rosalind Franklin solved the structure of DNA on her own, and her photograph was simply stolen by her Cambridge rivals
The structure of DNA emerged from several people's evidence and from two methods that each needed the other
X-ray diffraction alone settled the shape of DNA once the technique had been perfected at King's
The Nobel committee of 1962 wronged Franklin by applying its rules too strictly to a case that deserved an exception
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 1 says the model rested on measurements made by other people, and paragraph 12 names those contributions and calls the double helix the meeting point of two methods, neither of which would have finished the job alone. One choice holds both halves.

proof.quote: But the model rested on measurements made by other people
Those answers came from the symmetry in Franklin's crystallographic report, from Chargaff's ratios, from Donohue's chemistry
neither would have finished the job alone

distractorNotes: Reversed: paragraph 1 says the model rested on other people's measurements, and paragraph 12 names them.
This is the story paragraph 11 calls too simple; the passage says she was close, not finished.
Contradicted: paragraph 12 says how little a single image could settle.
Unsupported and too narrow: the Nobel rules are stated without blame, and the credit debate is only part of the passage.

answer.text: The structure of DNA emerged from several people's evidence and from two methods that each needed the other
answer.line: Paragraph 1 says the model rested on other people's measurements; paragraph 12 names them and says two methods needed each other.

steps: Read the frame and the close. Paragraph 1 sets up the question; paragraph 12 answers it.
The frame: the model "rested on measurements made by other people."
The close: answers from Franklin's report, Chargaff's ratios and Donohue's chemistry, then two methods, neither enough alone. Pick both halves.

choices.text: Watson and Crick deserve sole credit for the double helix because they alone were willing to build and test models
choices.note: Sole credit goes too far: paragraph 1 says their model rested on other people's measurements.

choices.note: Many hands from paragraph 1, two methods from paragraph 12.

choices.text: X-ray diffraction alone settled the shape of DNA once the technique had been perfected at King's
choices.note: Paragraph 12 opens on how little a single image could settle. Chemistry and model building were needed too.

choices.note: The author states the prize rules without blaming anyone. And one paragraph's detail cannot be the main idea of the whole passage.
